message: sample_id must be unique in samples.csv; joins would be ambiguous.
Collection date is after the reference date 2026-11-07.
AST result must be S, I or R. EUCAST I means susceptible, increased exposure; other standards may define categories differently.
The same aggregate-surveillance key appears more than once. Rows are never summed automatically because duplicates would double-count; remove the duplicate or add a field that distinguishes the rows.

Labels in 'organism' differ only by case/whitespace; they are merged onto the most frequent spelling for analysis. Synonyms (e.g. abbreviations) are not merged: curate a controlled vocabulary upstream.
Collection dates must be ISO 8601 (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). Other forms such as 05/06/2024 are ambiguous (day/month order) and are not parsed; the affected year is unknown.
Rows reference sample IDs absent from samples.csv; they are excluded from isolate-linked outputs.
Calls below identity 90% or coverage 60% are flagged for expert review. These are review flags, not call filters; no call is dropped for this reason.
Calls from heuristic-motif or generic homology-search methods are not validated resistance-gene detections. They are excluded from linkage and concordance by the configured evidence-tier policy.
AST rows without result cannot contribute to categorical indicators.
MIC must be a number, optionally with a censoring operator (<=, <, >, >=, =); decimal commas are not accepted. Original rows are retained for review.
An AST result is dated before its isolate's collection date.
